findings.claim: getForLogin caches the initial query with startupRevision instead of cache.getCurrentCounter() as the getByOrganization sibling does, so the login cache entry is created with a stale revision.
evidence: The query == null branch uses cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision), while the immediately following cached == null branch uses cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()), and the getByOrganization implementation at lines 193-203 shown in context uses cache.getCurrentCounter().

findings.claim: remove() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) at line 78 without a null check, and storedIdp can be null when the delegate has no IDP with that alias.
evidence: String cacheKey = cacheKeyIdpAlias(getRealm(), alias); IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias); is followed by registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) in the else-terminating path after the if/else block, with no null guard between them.
registerIDPLoginInvalidation and registerIDPInvalidation dereference the idp parameter (idp.getInternalId(), getLoginPredicate().test(idp)), so a null storedIdp causes an NPE.

findings.claim: registerIDPLoginInvalidation calls getLoginPredicate().test(idp), but the modified predicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard on the config map, causing an NPE for IDP models with a null config.
evidence: The new predicate in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getLoginPredicate() is idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)), which calls idp.getConfig().get(...) directly.
registerIDPLoginInvalidation at this line passes idp into getLoginPredicate().test(idp) for every create/remove, including IDPs whose getConfig() may be null.

findings.claim: The added predicate link idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, so it throws an NPE whenever getConfig() returns null.
evidence: The line calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) unconditionally; IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() can return null (e.g., freshly constructed models with no config set), unlike the sibling check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean which uses idp.getConfig().get(...) only after idp.isEnabled() filters.

Other usages in the same diff (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) call Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) inside isPublicOrganizationBroker, which has the same exposure, indicating the null-config case is reachable.

findings.claim: The predicate applies the BROKER_PUBLIC requirement to IDPs whose getOrganizationId() is non-null regardless of the search organizationId, so a login lookup for a different organization (or for any org) now drops non-public org IDPs that the delegate's getForLogin(mode, organizationId) would otherwise return for that mode.
evidence: getLoginPredicate() is a static filter combined into all getForLogin searches irrespective of the FetchMode or organizationId argument; the previous predicate was only Stream.of(values()).map(LoginFilter::getFilter).reduce(Predicate::and).get().

The OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean onlyOrganizationBrokers branch applies Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) itself, implying the predicate's role differed per mode before this change.

findings.claim: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate's early-return for !original && !updated skips invalidation even when the update changes the organizationId of an IDP currently unavailable for login, leaving stale login-cache results once that IDP's org linkage affects mode-filtered lists.
evidence: The method comment says 'In all other scenarios, the caches must be invalidated', but the first guard returns without comparing original.getOrganizationId() and updated.getOrganizationId().
The second guard compares organizationId only when both original and updated pass getLoginPredicate(), so an org-link change on a non-login IDP never reaches the invalidation loop.

findings.claim: remove() now fetches storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally even on the cached path where the CachedIdentityProvider is available, adding a delegate store read where the previous code only hit the delegate when isInvalid(cacheKey) was true.
evidence: The previous code only called idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) inside the isInvalid(cacheKey) branch; the new code hoists the call before the branch and uses cached.getIdentityProvider() in the else branch only for registerIDPInvalidation, discarding the already-fetched storedIdp on that path.

findings.claim: The re-check filter for the ORG_ONLY branch adds idp.isEnabled() but omits !idp.isLinkOnly() and !idp.isHideOnLogin() that the organization-specific branch at line 65 applies, so link-only or hide-on-login org IDPs can be rendered.
evidence: The this.organization != null branch filters idp.isEnabled() && !idp.isLinkOnly() && !idp.isHideOnLogin() && Boolean.parseBoolean(...), while the ORG_ONLY fallback branch right below only filters idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias()).
The comment on the changed line says the IDP might have been wrapped, which applies to isLinkOnly()/isHideOnLogin() exactly as it does to isEnabled().

findings.claim: The ALL branch's re-check filter adds idp.isEnabled() but omits !idp.isLinkOnly() and !idp.isHideOnLogin(), so wrapped IDPs that are link-only or hide-on-login still reach createIdentityProvider.
evidence: The changed line is .filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && !Objects.equals(existingIDP, idp.getAlias())) while the organization-specific branch at line 65 includes !idp.isLinkOnly() && !idp.isHideOnLogin() in its filter.
The wrapping performed by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (organization-aware model overriding isEnabled()) means isLinkOnly()/isHideOnLogin() semantics can also change after wrapping.

findings.claim: The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so none of the 20 created IDPs are actually removed by cleanup.
evidence: The loop creates IDPs with idpRep.setAlias("idp-alias-" + i) but the cleanup line reads getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove).

The method reference testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove is also evaluated eagerly at registration time on a nonexistent alias, and the resulting cleanup action targets the wrong resource.

findings.claim: The cleanup registration for idp-alias-20 uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-20", so the newly created IDP is not cleaned up.
evidence: The IDP was created with idpRep.setAlias("idp-alias-" + 20) but the cleanup line reads getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove).

findings.claim: The test removes idp-alias-1 with testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-1").remove() but asserts that login caches are NOT invalidated, contradicting the implementation since idp-alias-1 was created with setEnabled((i % 2) == 0) making i=1 disabled and thus not a login IDP per the new predicate only if hideOnLogin is also false; the assert cannot distinguish a correct skip from a broken invalidation because the removed IDP's config also lacks BROKER_PUBLIC.
evidence: The comment on the preceding lines says 'add/remove IDPs that are not available for login - none of these operations should invalidate the login caches', and the test then removes idp-alias-1 which is disabled per the creation loop.

registerIDPLoginInvalidation gates invalidation on getLoginPredicate().test(idp), which requires isEnabled() among other filters, so a disabled IDP skips invalidation; the assertion then passes, but the same assertion block also runs right after creating idp-alias-20 with setHideOnLogin(true), so the assert cannot fail to detect a create-path invalidation regression for the remove path independently.

findings.claim: After step 4 the test asserts getForLogin(FetchMode.ALL, orgaId) returns 11 IDPs, but idp-alias-20 was just moved from realm-level into the org while remaining in the REALM_ONLY count of 5, meaning the expected union count should be 5 + 6 = 11 only if idp-alias-20 is excluded from realm-only; the assertion as written assumes the implementation drops it from REALM_ONLY via the invalidation, which the separate addIdentityProvider call at line 485 does not necessarily trigger.
evidence: The test performs testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20").update(idpRep) (adding BROKER_PUBLIC config) and then testRealm().organizations().get(orgaId).identityProviders().addIdentityProvider("idp-alias-20") as two separate operations; the organization-link change happens in the second call, which is not the update() path handled by registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate.

The test then asserts all login caches are null, but the invalidation on org-linking depends on code paths (organization provider addIdentityProvider) not shown to call the IDP storage provider's update/create invalidation hooks in this diff.
